Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}

input: {
    "question": "user: What is a car lease?\nassistant: A lease is a type of credit agreement, which means that the lessor may not permit transfers. Essentially, a lease is a rental arrangement. You borrow money to cover the expected depreciation of the asset over the term of the lease. Generally, this arrangement will cost more over time compared to traditional ownership. However, leasing can be a sensible option if you prefer to drive a new car every two or three years.\nuser: In what circumstances is it better to lease than buy?\nassistant: Leasing a car can be more advantageous than buying because it transforms what would be a capital purchase—subject to depreciation for tax purposes—into a rental expense. Rental expenses can be deducted directly without the need for depreciation. However, if you are not operating a business that can take advantage of the tax benefits of leasing, then leasing may not be the best option for you.\nWhen you lease a car, you're essentially paying for the depreciation associated with a specific number of allowed miles, even if you don't actually drive that distance. While you can deduct your lease payments subject to certain limitations, having more expenses generally translates to lower profits. \nAs a rule of thumb, it's often advisable to BUY rather than lease unless you plan to use the vehicle for business purposes where you can write off lease payments. Many believe leasing is a disadvantageous choice; after all, leasing is essentially just renting, and dealerships typically prefer customers to lease.\nuser: Does the same kind of principle apply to any purchase? \nassistant: I apologize, but I do not have an answer to your question.\nuser: I completely understand; it is a very general question.\nassistant: Thank you!\nuser: Will I receive a tax deduction if I buy a property?\nassistant: The primary tax benefit of home ownership is the mortgage interest deduction, which applies to a portion of the interest you pay. It's important to note that deductions reduce your taxable income rather than your overall tax bill, and the savings from a deduction depend on your tax bracket. Many deductions, such as property tax and private mortgage insurance, are available only if you choose to itemize. Additionally, the property tax on your home may be nearly equal to the standard deduction, which makes this benefit less significant.\nuser: Rental property",
    "answer": "If you mean whether buying a rental property gives you a tax deduction, the document does not establish that. It does explain these rental-property rules:\n\n- If a home is partly your personal residence and partly rental property, you must allocate expenses—including mortgage, property tax and insurance—between the two uses, determine the rental portion’s value, and depreciate that portion under IRS rules. [S1]\n- If you use a dwelling as your personal residence and rent it for fewer than 15 days, you do not report the rental income or deduct expenses as rental expenses. [S2]\n- On sale, depreciation must be recaptured. [S4]\n\nThe document recommends professional tax advice and points to IRS Tax Topic 415 and Publication 527. [S2]"
}
